newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar down marginally on BOJ governor comments.
newsitem.headline: Dollar down marginally on BOJ governor comments.

text.p: 0139 GMT --*Dollar down marginally against yen in directionless mid-morning Tokyo trade following remarks by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita, dealers said.
*Matsushita told parliamentary committee on Thursday that it was important to take policy steps pre-emptively in order to realise continued growth without inflation.
*Market trapped between investor bids below 115.90 yen and persistent selling interest above 116.30 yen, dealers said.
*Market awaiting U.S. May jobs data due on Friday for clues to near-term direction.

*"The priority in monetary policy rests in stabilising prices for continued economic growth without inflation. At the same time, we believe it is important to act promptly on policy steps while keeping watch over asset prices and money supply movements," Matsushita said. 0012 GMT

*Dollar clings just above 116 yen in early Tokyo with downside solid near 115.80 yen due to possible bids from life insurers and talk of trust bank bids related to fresh foreign investment by pension funds.

*Japan posted customs-cleared trade surplus of 41.16 billion yen in fist 20 days of May, compared with deficit of 180.94 billion yen in the same period one year earlier, but impact on currencies limited.

*Mark/yen slightly lower but support seen near 67 yen flat with possible bids from trust banks, a city bank dealer said. But he said stop-loss sales may emerge near 66.95 yen and then 66.80 yen if mark decisively breaches 67 yen.
*Talk of possible dollar offers from European central banks near 1.7330 marks overnight, the city bank dealer said.
